initial_scene: The robot faces the tabletop from an oblique left-front view. A single electric kettle stands upright on the table, with its handle toward the robot and a small switch/control protruding below the handle. The far/right hand starts below the table edge; the near/left forearm and open hand remain low in front of the torso.

observed_sequence.action: Right hand begins low beside the tabletop edge; left arm stays bent low in the foreground. Kettle remains upright.
Right arm raises and reaches forward toward the kettle, with an extended finger aimed toward the lower handle/control area and the thumb separated below it.
Right hand advances closer and lowers its extended fingertip to the small control beneath the kettle handle. Contact is established around the lower handle area by the end of this interval.
Right fingertip remains at the switch/control region while the arm holds its reach; the robot neither grasps nor lifts the kettle. Left hand remains low without stabilizing the kettle.

Right hand makes a small downward/forward pressing movement at the lower handle switch. The kettle shifts/turns slightly while remaining upright on the table. Actual electrical activation is not distinguishable.
Right hand retracts away from the kettle and lowers toward its starting area. The kettle remains upright in its slightly adjusted position; left arm remains low and uninvolved.

arm_hand_roles.right: Active far-side arm: raises toward kettle, positions an extended finger at the lower-handle switch, presses/holds at that control region, then retracts. No kettle grasp or lift.
arm_hand_roles.left: Near-side arm remains bent low in the foreground with an open hand; it does not contact, support, or stabilize the kettle.
arm_hand_roles.coordination: Single-hand manipulation; no two-hand coordination or hand-to-hand transfer.

anatomical_side_evidence.description: The initial PNG shows the face and chest directed toward the table, viewed from the robot's left-front side. The large near shoulder and bent forearm form the anatomical left arm; the active hand connects through the farther arm/shoulder on the opposite side of the chest, establishing it as anatomical right. This follows the body attachment and facing direction rather than screen left/right.

terminal_state: At frame 363 the right hand has pulled away and is below/near the tabletop edge, clear of the kettle. The kettle remains upright on the tabletop, slightly shifted/turned from its initial pose. No visible boiling or unambiguous indicator change establishes electrical activation.
uncertainties: The fingertip and small lower-handle switch partially occlude each other, so exact switch travel and applied force cannot be measured visually.
No clear illuminated indicator, steam, or boiling is visible; successful start-boiling activation remains uncertain despite the completed pressing gesture.
source_annotation_assessment: The original instruction identifies the intended start-boiling switch press. Observed motion is consistent with that intention, but its statement about appropriate activation force is not verifiable from the clip and activation is not assumed in the usable prompt.

inspection_coverage.sampled_frames: Every second decoded frame, 0 through 362 inclusive; all 182 samples visually inspected in three contact sheets.

world_model_prompt: The humanoid extends its right hand toward the electric kettle and presses the small switch beneath the handle with an outstretched finger. After holding contact briefly, it pulls the hand back, leaving the kettle upright on the tabletop. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.
original_task_instruction: Pressing the start boiling button on an electric kettle with precise finger placement and appropriate force for button activation.

selected_segment.reason: Complete original single-task reference; no cropping or trimming requested.
